chunks: Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"When the Muhrim (person in Ihram) kills game, he is liable for its compensation and gives the game as charity to a poor person. If he returns and kills another game, the compensation is not upon him, and Allah will take retribution from him, and the retribution is in the Hereafter."

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: The pilgrim in the state of Ihram

ai.seo_question: What is the difference in compensation for a Muhrim killing game for the first time versus subsequent times?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib* clarifies the distinction between worldly legal liability (jaza') and spiritual accountability (naqimah) for a pilgrim who kills game. While the first offense requires compensatory charity to the poor, subsequent offenses waive the material penalty but incur divine retribution in the Hereafter, highlighting the transition from juristic obligation to spiritual consequence.
